rounds.text: DC Infotech & Communication Ltd demonstrates robust top-line momentum, evidenced by a 34% compounded sales growth over 5 years and a 33% growth in the trailing twelve months [E14, E16]. This operational expansion is matched by exceptional profitability, highlighted by a 58% compounded profit growth over 5 years and a 47% growth in the trailing twelve months [E17, E19]. Capital efficiency metrics remain exceptionally strong, with a current return on equity of 23.7% and a ROCE of 23.0% [E12, E13]. Furthermore, intrinsic valuation models indicate substantial upside, with a discounted cash flow suggesting an intrinsic value of Rs 523 per share against a market price of Rs 292, offering a 44.2% margin of safety [E40, E41]. Institutional confidence is underscored by foreign institutions increasing their stake to 1.16% in June 2026 from 0.00% in September 2023, alongside promoter ownership rising to 62.20% [E37, E38]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -37 Cr in March 2026, leading to a weak cash conversion of -1.76x [E30, E31].

Conceded: compounded sales growth stands at 34% over 5 years and 33% in the trailing twelve months [E14, E16], alongside compounded profit growth of 58% and 47% [E17, E19]. Conceded: return on equity and ROCE sit at healthy levels of 23.7% and 23.0% [E12, E13], and intrinsic value models project upside [E40, E41]. However, this reported operational growth stands in stark contrast to a severe liquidity drain, evidenced by operating cash flow collapsing to negative Rs -37 Cr and free cash flow dropping to negative Rs -43 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32]. This disconnect yields an alarming cash conversion ratio of -1.76x, meaning reported profits completely fail to translate into actual cash generation [E30]. To finance this deficit, borrowings surged from Rs 51 Cr to Rs 87 Cr within a single year [E35], driving debt-to-equity to 0.81x [E34] while screeners explicitly warn that earnings growth is decelerating [E61]. Furthermore, despite rising promoter and foreign institutional stakes [E37, E38], the underlying equity carries a heavy annualised volatility of 62.8% and a brutal historical drawdown of -53.2% [E48, E49].
